newsitem.title: USA: Metromedia International to sell assets to MGM Inc.
newsitem.headline: Metromedia International to sell assets to MGM Inc.

text.p: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc. is buying Metromedia International Group Inc.'s entertainment group and film library for $573 million, the companies said Monday.

They said the deal involves Metromedia's 2,200-title film and television library and the production and distribution activities of its entertainment group, which includes Orion Pictures Corp., Goldwyn Entertainment Co. and Motion Picture Corp. of America.
In addition to the library, MGM will acquire 12 completed films and five direct-to-video features for future release.
The companies said the transaction does not include Metromedia's Landmark Theatre Group, which has a total of 138 screens at 50 locations throughout the United States.

After the acquisition, MGM's combined libraries will consist of more than 3,600 titles, including Oscar-winning films "Dances With Wolves," "The Silence of the Lambs," "The Best Years of Our Lives," "Wuthering Heights," "Guys and Dolls," and the "RoboCop" series.

The transaction is subject to the execution of a definitive agreement, approval by Metromedia's directors and stockholders, approval by MGM's board and stockholders, and satisfaction of other customary conditions.
